answer: Behavioral mirror clustering detects sybils post hoc by comparing each identity’s transaction timing and counterparty mix against a learned sonnet of normal activity, flagging near-duplicate behavioral signatures. Any cluster whose internal similarity exceeds a threshold triggers retroactive score decay, so every clone drags its siblings’ reputation down with it in a widening spiral. The attacker then pays a per-identity cost: each additional fake identity must sustain distinct, costly behavior for months or forfeit accumulated standing.
